findings.failure_path: A tool call is admitted under generation N and starts validation or preparation; revocation then advances to N+1; because the call has already “started,” it is not covered by the stated fence/cancel rule, and the text does not require an atomic generation recheck at the irreversible-handler entry, so the stale call can still perform the revoked side effect.
findings.smallest_fix: Define side-effect admission as the irreversible-handler commit boundary and serialize its final generation check with revocation using the same lock/fence. Require every call to recheck immediately before crossing that boundary, so ordering is unambiguous: revocation first rejects it; admission first gives revocation a defined drain/commit outcome and terminal receipt.

challenge_focus: Fresh full adversarial pass on the post-fix lane-5 candidate, not a confirm-my-fixes pass: (1) the shared serialization boundary between revocation and side-effect admission — an accepted-but-not-started call that still enters an irreversible handler, or a fence that loses accepted work; (2) one-bounded-slice-per-worker width and effort_budget — a multi-task worker that still slips through, or a rule that blocks a legitimate single slice with related items; (3) both-orders pairwise judging — a design that still claims an inconsistency rate without per-pair counterfactuals; (4) eviction-vs-invalidation, normalized cache counters, batch capability decision, plan-then-execute binding, fan-out read-only carve-out — any surviving contradiction; (5) authorization records, register anchors, receipts, rows — unsupported claims, stale locators, a row citing two owners; (6) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
predecessor_challenge_focuses: Adversarial pass on the lane-5 candidate: (1) atomic generation advance and re-authorization — an ordering where an in-flight completion is accepted before the generation advances, or a re-authorization that checks the tool but not destination, arguments, or data scope; (2) eviction-vs-invalidation, normalized cache counters, batch capability decision, tool-set boundary, plan-then-execute binding — any surviving path to a revoked call, a double count, duplicate billing, in-flight mutation, or an injected external action; (3) the fan-out gate's shared-write versus read-only distinction, effort_budget, artifact-not-relay, MAST classification, hub-vs-peer default — bypass-by-omission or over-broad cost; (4) register anchors, receipts, rows — stale locators, unsupported claims, contradictions, a row citing two owners; (5) vendor numbers as invariants, wrong ids, leakage.
